findings.claim: kmctl's README Upgrade section said auditing moved to kmaudit, but kmctl's own audit still ships.

verdict.text: The Upgrade section now says kmctl's own audit is unchanged and that kmaudit is a new, separate package you install apart.
That agrees with the README's intro, its `/audit` entry and the shipped code.
The gates are green and nothing else changed.
`loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval-row r1 all pass; stamp green c5667b7b6b06b5afa2b78a4e45863eb708296196c5eb37852c0b98c8a69046e5.

The new sentence at packages/kmctl/README.md:222-226 against the code: `action.yml` still has `mode: audit` and the `audit:` input (docs-vs-code), and `packages/kmctl/apm/.apm/skills/audit` and `agents/kmctl-auditor.md` still exist, so "unchanged" is true.
The description of kmaudit matches the first lines of packages/kmaudit/README.md.
Against the rest of the README: the intro (lines 12-18) calls the audit agent opt-in and says kmctl and kmaudit "install apart"; the `/audit` entry (line 314) still describes kmctl's own audit.
The staged diff: the only change since round 1 is that README paragraph.
The steps, the how-to and the tests are as they were in round 1.
f1: resolved at packages/kmctl/README.md:222-226, which now says kmctl's own audit is unchanged and kmaudit is a new, separate package.

The docstring of `test_upgrade_docs_send_auditing_to_kmaudit` (packages/kmctl/tests/test_docs.py) still calls kmaudit "the new home of auditing", which repeats the overstatement f1 fixed in the README.
The round 2 fix did not touch it, so it falls outside this narrow round.
It is worth rewording in a later pass, to something like "kmctl's README links kmaudit's README".
